answer: The system embeds each agent’s reputation in a cryptographic kernel that issues a signed river token proportional to verified work, like nectar for a pollinator. When a new identity joins, it must acquire river tokens by contributing proofs, and the kernel applies quadratic weighting so k fresh tokens yield only √k influence, so many Sybils are cheap in number but expensive in work. Thus an attacker must spend as much proof‑of‑work as a single honest agent to match its influence, turning a flood of fake IDs into a costly nectar harvest.
